new_sections.Method Overview: WildOS incrementally builds a sparse navigation graph from geometric sensing. ExploRFM processes camera images and text queries to predict visual traversability, visual frontiers, and open-vocabulary object similarity over a long-range visual horizon. Object detections from multiple viewpoints are fused by a probabilistic goal triangulation module to estimate coarse 3D target locations beyond sensor range. Geometric frontier nodes are scored using these visual-semantic cues, and a hierarchical planner selects actions over the scored graph. Closed-loop experiments show significant improvement over purely geometric and purely vision-based baselines.

new_sections.Function: ExploRFM processes the current image and a text query to output confidence maps for traversability (inverse jet colormap), visual frontiers (jet colormap), and object similarity. These outputs are used to score frontier nodes in the navigation graph.

new_sections.Purpose: To localize distant semantic goals (e.g., 'house') that are beyond the robot's depth horizon. The module uses a particle filter to maintain a distribution of possible goal positions, updated each time the robot observes the target from a new viewpoint.
